correctness.rationale: For normalized symmetric path adjacency S on M+1 vertices (M≥1), the cosine eigenvectors have squared vertex amplitudes d_j cos²(πkj/M)/M for k=1,...,M−1 and d_j/(2M) at modes 0,M. In the eigenbasis, consecutive-time observability is a Vandermonde matrix times diagonal amplitudes: determinant Gramian = V_φ·∏|v_k(j)|² for any injective spectral φ. With g=gcd(j,M), if M/g even exactly g amplitude columns vanish, yielding rank M+1−g and zero determinant; otherwise the root-of-unity cosine product is 2^{g−M}, giving the stated d_j^{M+1}2^{2(g−M)} ratio. For interior nonzero determinant g≤M/3, so strict endpoint improvement when M≥4; M=3 all four vertices tie, and M=1,2 only endpoints. Chebyshev–Lobatto discriminant gives endpoint determinant 2^{1−M²} at φ(s)=s. Independently verified the arithmetic determinant ratios and rank-parity/optimizer classification for all 65 sensor positions M=1,...,10; proof is analytic all M.
